That worry is real - if you try to cover all Cameroonians in all 50 states day one, the app feels empty everywhere. The fix is to stop thinking "United States" and start thinking "pockets". You own one city first, then expand. Here’s the streamlined V3 plan that solves the state problem: 1. Launch city by city, not state by state Pick 1-2 cities where you know Cameroonians already gather. Lowell and Worcester from your context are perfect starting points. You only show events in a 50 mile radius of the user’s location. A Cameroonian in Texas never sees empty Boston listings and vice versa. 2. Make the user tell you their tribe + location on signup When someone logs in, ask two things: country of origin - Cameroon, Nigeria, Ghana etc - and zip code. Now their feed is auto-filtered to Cameroonian events within 50 miles. No searching, no noise. If they move or travel, they can change the radius or city in settings. 3. Let users create events but keep it light No long forms. Event name, flyer upload, date, city. Then the “I dey go / I no sure / I no dey go” buttons you mentioned. The social proof of seeing 12 other Cameroonians in Lowell say they’re going is what gets people to show up. 4. Solve the empty room problem by seeding Before launch, you or 3 friends post the next 5 real events you know about - church meetings, meetups, parties. An empty app kills itself. 10 real events beats 100 fake ones. This way you don’t manage all states. The app manages it by geography and tribe. You just focus on getting Lowell/Worcester Cameroonians active first. Once that pocket is popping, you replicate it in Houston, Atlanta, etc. Quick question: Do you already know 20-30 Cameroonians in Lowell or Worcester you could invite to test V3? If yes, we can build the website version this week and test it with them before writing a line of app code.

YES. That is actually the perfect V3. Forget the whole US for now - own Massachusetts first.

Massachusetts is small enough for you to manage, but big enough to prove the idea. And North Shore / South Shore / Central is exactly how Africans here actually think and travel.

Nobody from Brockton is driving to Lowell for a party on a Friday. But they WILL drive from Brockton to Randolph (South Shore).

Here's how to do it for V3:

Your Massachusetts Pockets

Don't do 50 states. Do 5 zones in ONE state:

  1. Boston Metro - Boston, Cambridge, Somerville
  2. North Shore - Lowell, Lawrence, Lynn, Salem, Townsend area
  3. South Shore - Brockton, Randolph, Quincy, Dorchester
  4. Central Mass - Worcester, Fitchburg, Leominster
  5. Western Mass - Springfield, Holyoke

When a Cameroonian signs up in Lowell (01469), he automatically only sees North Shore + Boston Metro events. Not South Shore. No clutter.

How you build it so you don't go crazy:

On sign-up:
"Where you dey stay?" -> Dropdown: North Shore / South Shore / Boston / Central / Western

Then on the home feed:

  • Filter by default to their zone
  • But with tabs at top: [ My Zone ] [ All Mass ] [ Add Event ]

So if they want to see what's happening in Worcester for the weekend, they can still tap "All Mass" but their daily view is clean.

The real win for you:

You live in Townsend. You KNOW North Shore. You can personally go to 2 events this month, take pictures, post them on Parrot Vibes, and tag people who tapped "I Dey Go". That's how you make it feel alive.

You cannot do that for Texas from here. But you CAN dominate North Shore Cameroonian events in 30 days.

V3 launch plan:

  • Week 1: Build a simple website: parrotvibes.com - just 1 page with zones filter. Cost $0.
  • Week 2: You + 2 friends manually add the next 10 REAL Cameroonian / African events you know in North Shore and Boston for September.
  • Week 3: Invite 30 Cameroonians you know in Lowell / Worcester to the site. Ask them to tap "I Dey Go" on one event.
  • Week 4: Now you have proof. People see faces, not empty pages.

If that works in North Shore, you just copy/paste the same system to South Shore next month. Then you have a Massachusetts playbook you can sell to Houston, Atlanta, DMV.

Here's exactly how to deploy camairconnect.com Option 1 - step by step, 10 minutes:

PART 1: Create Supabase (your database - FREE)

  1. Go to supabase.com → Sign up with khumbahtung@gmail.com

  2. Click New Project

    • Name: camairconnect

    • Region: US East
    • Click Create (wait 1 min)

    • Copy Project URL → looks like https://xxxx.supabase.co

SQL
sql
create table events (id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(), title text, city text, zone text, date date, category text, flyer_url text, owner_email text, owner_name text, attendees text[] default '{}', rating_up int default 0, rating_down int default 0, rated_by text[] default '{}', created_at timestamp default now());create table comments (id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(), event_id uuid references events(id) on delete cascade, name text, text text, created_at timestamp default now());create table profiles (id uuid primary key, email text, name text, is_banned boolean default false);alter table events enable row level security; alter table comments enable row level security; alter table profiles enable row level security;create policy "public all" on events for all using (true) with check (true);create policy "public all" on comments for all using (true) with check (true);create policy "public all" on profiles for all using (true) with check (true);-- storage for flyersinsert into storage.buckets (id, name, public) values ('flyers','flyers', true) on conflict do nothing;create policy "public flyers read" on storage.objects for select using (bucket_id='flyers');create policy "public flyers upload" on storage.objects for insert with check (bucket_id='flyers');
